column1: # Test run schedule for run_all_tests.sh and run_all_tests.ps1.
# class   exclusive  runs alone, before the others, on an otherwise idle
#                    machine: a check depends on elapsed wall-clock time,
#                    or the test saturates every core.
#         wide:N     takes N of the --jobs run slots and shares the
#                    machine: the test keeps about N cores busy (renders
#                    larger than one 32-px tile, small thread pools) and
#                    nothing it checks depends on timing.  N is its measured
#                    mean cores rounded up.  Wide tests start first, the
#                    widest first, and pool / single tests fill the slots
#         single     takes one slot with its render threads forced to one
#                    repo's global.options): its renders spread over a few
#                    cores without gaining much throughput, and nothing it
#                    checks depends on the thread count.
#         pool       takes one slot as it is (the default for any test not
# seconds run time in a full `--jobs 10` run on a 10-core Apple M1 Max
#         (2026-11-18), only used to order the tests longest first.  The
#         runners prefer the time each test took in this checkout's last
#         run (bin/.test_timings.tsv).  Pool tests under 5 s are not listed.
# reason  why the test is exclusive, wide or single.  "N cores" is the
#         measured mean over the test (or its first 60 s), with the peak
#         3-s window; "on one thread" times were measured with other tests
# The runner's summary lists tests that kept more cores busy than their
# slots; give such a test a wide:N entry.  A new test that checks a timing
